rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence confirms the refuge command and explains it: when Satan's prompting is sensed, refuge is the response; its opening إن marks importance, not denial or doubt.
rows.anchor: هذا تأكيد وتقرير للأمر بالاستعاذة من الشيطان ، فتتنزل جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's protection delivers the Messenger from Satan's prompting and recalls the duty to struggle against Satan and stay alert to his schemes.
rows.anchor: أولاهما أن الاستعاذة بالله منجاة للرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام من نزغ الشيطان ، والثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is commanded to resist Satan because he is pious and takes joy in following the example of earlier pious people, as in 6:90.
rows.anchor: فالرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام مأمور بمجاهدة الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory reason is broader than the command it explains, since remembrance covers more than seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: وقد جاءت العلة هنا أعم من المعلل : لأن التذكر أعم من الاستعاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur conjectures that this community was specially given the practice of seeking refuge, repeatedly commanded in the Qur'an and Prophet's sayings, while earlier peoples were given remembrance, as this community was given Friday.
rows.anchor: ولعل الله ادخر خصوصية الاستعاذة لهذه الأمة ، فكثر في القرآن الأمر بالاستعاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious here are the messengers and the righteous among their communities, presented as exemplary models; taqwa was explained at 2:2.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم : الرسل وصالحو أممهم ، لأنه أريد جعلهم قدوة وأسوة حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mass literally means placing a hand on a body and is used metaphorically for affliction, including the slightest contact.
rows.anchor: و ( المس ) حقيقته وضع اليد على الجسم ، واستعير للإصابة أو لأدنى الإصابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ta'if is a visitor who circles a place awaiting permission to enter; the word depicts a satanic thought at its first circulation in the mind.
rows.anchor: والطائف هو الذي يمشي حول المكان ينتظر الإذن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab custom had an arriving guest circle the household and seek leave and hospitality; Ibn Ashur cites the story of al-Nabigha with al-Nu'man as an example.
rows.anchor: وكانت عادة العرب أن القادم إلى أهل البيت ، العائذ برب البيت ، المستأنس للقرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The custom of circumambulating the Kaaba imitates guests approaching a household; it may explain using طائف for a hidden, fleeting visitation.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك طواف القادمين إلى مكة بالكعبة تشبها بالوافدين على المملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's line uses طائف for a visitation by a jinn apparition, and Qur'an 68:19 calls a calamity a طائف.
rows.anchor: ألم بها من طائف الجن أولق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read طائف with an alif and hamza; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read طيف, without the alif and with a silent yāʾ, meaning a dream image familiar in poetry.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب : ( طيف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إذا and light-touch verb point to seeking God at the first onset of satanic thoughts, before they grow into resolve and action.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الفزع إلى الله من الشيطان ، عند ابتداء إلمام الخواطر الشيطانية بالنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite noun may mean devils generically or refer to Iblis, since his army's whispering is attributed to his command and authority.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون تعريف الجنس : أي من الشياطين ويجوز أن يكون تعريف العهد والمراد به إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering is bringing prior knowledge to mind, especially God's commands; it can include recalling refuge if that practice was prescribed to earlier peoples and is prescribed to this community.
rows.anchor: والتذكر استحضار المعلوم السابق ، والمراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the pious includes recollecting and carrying out all commanded duties, not just seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: فالاقتداء بالذين اتقوا يعم سائر أحوال التذكر للمأمورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result-fāʾ and sudden إذا stress immediate insight: once firm remembrance occurs, they quickly see the truth, leave the satanic thought, and act by what they remembered.
rows.anchor: وأكد معنى ( فاء ) التعقيب ب ( إذا ) الفجائية الدالة على حصول مضمون جملتها دفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction carries the address forward from 7:203: the Messenger is to tell the polytheists, explicitly or implicitly, not to turn away from hearing and considering the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يؤذن العطف بأن الخطاب بالأمر في قوله : { فاستمعوا وأنصتوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning targets polytheists who refused to listen and urged one another to make noise, as described in 41:26; the Qur'an is a great sign, insight, guidance, and mercy for believers.
rows.anchor: وقد علم من أحوال المشركين أنهم كانوا يتناهون عن الإنصات إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the Qur'an again instead of using a pronoun honors it, emphasizes the instruction, and lets the sentence stand independently, a recognized eloquent usage.
rows.anchor: وذكر اسم القرآن إظهار في مقام الإضمار ، لأن القرآن تقدم ذكره بواسطة اسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istima is attentive listening, with its derived form suggesting intensity; insat means listening while stopping speech, adding silence to the command to listen.
rows.anchor: والاستماع الإصغاء وصيغة الافتعال دالة على المبالغة في الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istima may also be figurative for heeding and acting on the Qur'an, as in 7:198; insat then combines attentive listening with abandoning frivolous speech.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاستماع مستعملا في معناه المجازي ، وهو الامتثال للعمل بما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes disbelievers as those being admonished and Muslims as those being guided; believers are especially likely to benefit, following 7:203.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخطاب شامل للكفار على وجه التبليغ ، وللمسلمين على وجه الارشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse belongs with the preceding Meccan verses whether its direct audience is both groups, Muslims explicitly and polytheists implicitly, or polytheists for guidance and Muslims all the more.
rows.anchor: ولا شبهة في أن هذه الآية نزلت في جملة الآيات التي قبلها وعلى مناسبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listening and silence should lead to reflection, inference, faith in the Messenger, and reform of the soul through the Qur'an; the command invites proclamation, thought, and action, at levels suited to each hearer.
rows.anchor: فالاستماع والإنصات المأمور بهما هما المؤديان بالسامع إلى النظر والاستدلال ، والاهتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is general in wording only imperfectly: context and the anti-listening response in 41:26 clarify part of its scope, with other cases settled by further evidence.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية مجملة في معنى الاستماع والإنصات وفي مقتضى الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree the verse's apparent wording is interpreted in many situations; it cannot require every Muslim to stop work and listen whenever anyone recites nearby.
rows.anchor: وقد اتفق علماء الأمة على أن ظاهر الآية بمجرده في صور كثيرة مؤول

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A reported interpretation says the verse concerns hearing the imam recite aloud in prayer.
rows.anchor: فرووا عن أبي هريرة أنها نزلت في قراءة الإمام في الجهر

rows.speaker: رجل من الأنصار
rows.claim: Another report says an Ansari prayed behind the Prophet in an audible prayer and recited while the Prophet recited, prompting the command to listen to the imam.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا من الأنصار صلى وراء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة جهرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects restricting the command to an imam's recitation: the occasion report is unsound, does not fit the verse's arrangement, and is interpretation rather than a Prophetic transmission.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل ضعيف ، لأن نزول الآية على هذا السبب لم يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Maliki tendency is to retain a near-general command but treat it as recommended; Ibn Ashur says it would be better to mean the Messenger's recitation to people so they may know and act on the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من أبقى أمر الاستماع على إطلاقه القريب من العموم ، ولكنهم تأولوه على أمر الندب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi quotes Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: when the polytheists came as the Prophet prayed, they told one another not to listen and to make noise, and this verse answered them.
rows.anchor: وفي ( تفسير القرطبي ) عن سعيد ( بن المسيب ) : كان المشركون يأتون رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says the proposed occasions do not fit: this verse is Meccan, whereas those incidents occurred in Medina.
rows.anchor: على أن ما تقدم من الاخبار في محمل سبب نزول هذه الآية لا يستقيم لأن الآية مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not support the Hanafi argument for a follower to omit recitation when the imam recites silently, because that omission is not listening and silence.
rows.anchor: فالآية بمعزل عنه إذ لا يتحقق في ذلك الترك معنى الإنصات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affirmative verbs قرئ and استمعوا do not themselves carry a general sense, so the verse contains no explicit formula of generality.
rows.anchor: ليس في الآية صيغة من صيغ العموم لأن الذي فيها فعلان هما ( قرىء ) ( واستمعوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا generalizes circumstances or times, not kinds of recitation; generality of time or circumstance does not itself entail generality across people.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الشرط المستفاد من ( إذا ) يقتضي إلا عموم الأحوال أو الأزمان دون القراءات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the commands the Prophet must convey, the discourse turns to his own devotion; asking people to hear the Qur'an implies his reciting it aloud, then his own remembrance is addressed.
rows.anchor: إقبال بالخطاب على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يختص به ، بعد أن أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean the life-giving soul, the embodied self, inner cognition, or a person's private self; 5:116 uses it for what lies within, and the Bukhari hadith contrasts it with a public gathering.
rows.anchor: ولكون مقر النفس في باطن الإنسان أطلقت على أمور باطن الإنسان من الإدراك والعقل

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A hadith qudsi in Sahih al-Bukhari says God reciprocates a servant's private remembrance privately and remembrance in an assembly in a better assembly.
rows.anchor: وإن ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي وإن ذكرني في ملإ ذكرته في ملإ خير منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God in solitude as you remember Him among people.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : اذكر ربك وأنت في خلوتك كما تذكره في مجامع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr here is verbal and includes Qur'an and other speech praising or thanking God, such as the testimony of faith, hawqala, tasbih, takbir, and supplication.
rows.anchor: والذكر حقيقة في ذكر اللسان ، وهو المراد هنا ، ويعضده قوله : { ودون الجهر من القول }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadarru means humility, which Arabs conventionally associate with raised speech; it alludes to raising the voice both literally and figuratively, as in 7:55.
rows.anchor: و ( التضرع ) التذلل ولما كان التذلل يستلزم الخطاب بالصوت المرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khifa is a verbal noun for fear; its morphological form is not meant to depict a particular posture or manner.
rows.anchor: وقوبل التضرع هنا بالخيفة وهي اسم مصدر الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since fear is an inward reaction and makes one speak softly lest the feared one notice, khifa alludes here to quiet speech motivated by fear of God.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الخيفة انفعالا نفسيا يجده الإنسان في خاصة نفسه كانت مستلزمة للتخافت بالكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing is an antithesis in both direct and allusive senses: humility with voicing and fear with secrecy.
rows.anchor: فمقابلتها بالتضرع طباق في معنيي اللفظين الصريحين ومعنييهما الكناءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase denotes a middle volume, between loudness and secrecy; the verse thereby covers all modes of verbal remembrance, since people feel more energy for some than others.
rows.anchor: وهو الذكر المتوسط بين الجهر والإسرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghudu is morning, the first half of the day.
rows.anchor: اسم لزمن الصباح وهو النصف الأول من النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asal is the plural of asil, meaning evening, the second half of the day until sunset.
rows.anchor: جمع أصيل وهو العشي وهو النصف الثاني من النهار إلى الغروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two terms cover the conventional span of daylight; night is generally for sleep, while waking hours receive special instruction such as 73:2 and also fall under the ban on heedlessness.
rows.anchor: والمقصود استيعاب أجزاء النهار بحسب المتعارف ، فأما الليل فهو زمن النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns neglecting God's remembrance, but negligence has no fixed measure, since the Prophet's own circumstances include receiving revelation and ordinary needs such as eating.
rows.anchor: فدل قوله : { ولا تكن من الغافلين } على التحذير من الغفلة عن ذكر الله ولاحد للغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command is specifically addressed to the Prophet; the community should emulate what is obligatory for him unless they are prohibited from it, as with continuous fasting.
rows.anchor: وهذا الأمر خاص بالرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ، وكل ما خص به الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying 'do not be among the heedless' is stronger than 'do not be heedless': it warns against joining a group characterized by heedlessness and makes the prohibited state clearer.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أن نحو { ولا تكن من الغافلين } أشد في الانتفاء وفي النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment says the remaining readers pronounce the preceding hamza with kasra; its antecedent is not repeated in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الباقون بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's concluding generalization also explains its preceding clause: a general conclusion can serve as the major premise supporting the specific point.
rows.anchor: لأن التذييل لما فيه من العموم يصلح لإفادة تعليل المذيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing the care and victory that followed their reluctant departure for Badr, God commands obedience in gratitude and warns them against disobedience, since the Messenger's commands bring good outcomes.
rows.anchor: لما أراهم الله آيات لطفه وعنايته بهم ، ورأوا فوائد امتثال أمر الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed obedience command returns to 8:1 as a sermon returns to its opening premise, now serving as the conclusion after the argument about Badr, obedience, divine aid, and defeat of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا رجوع إلى الأمر بالطاعة الذي افتتحت به السورة في قوله : { وأطيعوا الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative separates the renewed command from what precedes, marking it as the concluding lesson after the extended admonition.
rows.anchor: فذلكة للمقصود من الموعظة الواقعة بطولها عقب قوله : { وأطيعوا الله ورسوله إن كنتم مؤمنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here لو expresses entailment more than an unreal condition: their turning away is already established, and they would still turn away even if God granted the special hearing of understanding.
rows.anchor: بل المعنى على أنهم يتولون حتى في حالة ما لو سمعهم الله الإسماع المخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial nominal clause attaches to the pronoun in تولوا and explains that turning as figurative turning away.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { وهم معرضون } حال من ضمير تولوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal form signals settled refusal; some turn away temporarily and later return, as Mus'ab ibn Umayr did before accepting Islam.
rows.anchor: وصوغ هذه الجملة بصيغة الجملة الاسمية للدلالة على تمكن إعراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summons restates 8:20 after the sura's case for obedience: Badr showed its blessings, and the commands to stand firm, obey, and heed the Messenger lead to this concluding appeal.
rows.anchor: إعادة لمضمون قوله : { يأيها الذين ءامنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's call gives life to the community, and responding to him gives hearts sacred powers.
rows.anchor: فإن في دعوته إياهم إحياء لنفوسهم وأعلمهم أن الله يكسب قلوبهم بتلك الاستجابة قوى قدسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life literally enables bodily perception and voluntary movement; metaphorically it is a quality that completes a thing's purpose, as plant growth animates land and knowledge and sound judgment animate intellect.
rows.anchor: والحياة قوة بها يكون الإدراك والتحرك بالاختيار ويستعار الإحياء تبعا لاستعارة الحياة للصفة أو القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life and giving life can also mean preserving life by warding off its threats, as in the life-giving value of retribution and saving one person, cited at 2:179 and 5:32.
rows.anchor: وتستعار الحياة والإحياء لبقاء الحياة واستبقائها بدفع العوادي عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here life is what perfects human beings: sound belief, noble character, guidance to good action, reform of individuals and society, courage, independence, freedom, and stable livelihood.
rows.anchor: وهو إعطاء الإنسان ما به كمال الإنسان ، فيعم

words: استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must answer the Messenger whether he asks them to come or calls for an action; 'for what gives you life' explains the benefit rather than limiting the call, since his summons always brings some human good.
rows.anchor: فالآية تقتضي الأمر بالامتثال لما يدعو إليه الرسول سواء دعا حقيقة بطلب القدوم ، أم طلب عملا من الأعمال

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
rows.claim: A report cited from the Sahih collections says Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla was praying in the mosque, did not answer the Prophet's call, then heard the verse cited before being taught the greatest surah, al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بنن المعلى ، قال : كنت أصلي في المسجد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Ka'b during prayer; Ubayy finished, and the Prophet cited the verse when asking why he had not answered.
rows.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج على أبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cites the command through إذا دعاكم, which supports Ibn Ashur's reading of لما يحييكم as an explanatory qualifier, not a restriction on which calls must be answered.
rows.anchor: فوقفه على قوله : { إذا دعاكم } يدل على أن { لما يحييكم } قيد كاشف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Ubayy report is also transmitted by Malik ibn Anas; Ibn Ashur clarifies that this is the same report found in al-Tirmidhi.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وهو مروي أيضا من طريق مالك بن أنس

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a similar incident with Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman during the Battle of the Trench; Ibn Ashur says multiple similar cases underline the special status of the Messenger's call.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية وروي أنه وقع نحوه مع حذيفة بن اليمان في غزوة الخندق
